feed.title: Finance, Markets & Crypto — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Bitcoin Developer Documentation
entry.summary: A developer guide and reference for building on Bitcoin: transactions, RPC and the P2P network. Unlike the white paper it is practical documentation.

entry.title: Bitcoin Stack Exchange
entry.summary: A Q&A site for Bitcoin users and developers. Unlike forums, answers are voted and edited, so the good one rises to the top.

entry.title: Bitcoin Whitepaper
entry.summary: The nine-page paper that introduced Bitcoin. Unlike secondary explanations it is the source: short, readable, and the text every later claim should be checked against.

entry.title: Bitcoin Wiki
entry.summary: The community wiki on how Bitcoin works: protocol, script, history. Unlike news sites it is a maintained reference, not dated articles.

entry.title: CCXT
entry.summary: A library giving one API over more than a hundred crypto exchanges (JavaScript, Python, PHP and others). Unlike each exchange’s own SDK you write once and switch exchange freely.

entry.title: CoinCap
entry.summary: Crypto prices and market-cap rankings, with the data also available through a free API. Unlike busier trackers it is a plain table with direct data access.

entry.title: CoinDesk
entry.summary: A crypto and blockchain news site with market data and analysis. Unlike aggregators such as CryptoPanic it does its own reporting.

entry.title: CryptoPanic
entry.summary: A crypto news aggregator that marks headlines by their expected effect on price. Unlike a single news site it gathers many sources into one feed.

entry.title: Electrum
entry.summary: A lightweight open-source Bitcoin wallet, developed since 2011. Unlike full-node wallets it does not download the chain — you gain speed and trade some trust in servers for it.

entry.title: Ethplorer
entry.summary: An Ethereum token explorer: holders, transfers and token pages. Unlike Etherscan it centres on tokens and their holder distribution.

entry.title: MetaMask
entry.summary: The most widely used browser-extension wallet for Ethereum-compatible networks. Unlike hardware wallets the keys live in software on your device: convenient, but only as safe as your machine.

entry.title: OpenZeppelin
entry.summary: Audited smart-contract libraries and security tooling for Solidity. Unlike writing token or access-control contracts yourself, they are building blocks tested in wide use.

entry.title: WhatToMine
entry.summary: A calculator comparing the profitability of GPU-mineable coins from your hashrate, power draw and electricity price. Unlike general price trackers it computes mining profit directly.

entry.title: Awesome AI in Finance
entry.summary: A list of tools, data and papers solving finance problems with machine learning. Unlike general finance lists it focuses on the AI intersection.

entry.title: Awesome Algorand
entry.summary: A list of developer resources for Algorand, a proof-of-stake blockchain. Unlike Ethereum lists, it focuses on a pure proof-of-stake chain and its smart-contract tooling.

entry.title: Awesome Billing
entry.summary: A list of engineering resources for payments, invoicing, pricing and accounting. Unlike a single payment provider’s docs it is vendor-neutral and covers the field’s traps — rounding, tax, currencies.

entry.title: Awesome Bitcoin
entry.summary: A list of services and tools for Bitcoin software development. Unlike general crypto lists, it focuses only on Bitcoin: libraries, node software, wallets, APIs.

entry.title: Awesome Bitcoin Payment Processors
entry.summary: A list of processors and tools to start accepting Bitcoin payments. Unlike general payment lists, it focuses on Bitcoin only and sets self-hosted solutions beside custodial processors.

entry.title: Awesome Coins
entry.summary: A list of cryptocurrency tools and algorithms — wallets, node software, libraries. Unlike price sites it collects the underlying technology, not the product.

entry.title: Awesome Cosmos
entry.summary: A resource list for Cosmos, a modular framework for building app-specific blockchains. Unlike writing smart contracts on Ethereum, you build your own application-specific chain with the Cosmos SDK.

entry.title: Awesome Credit Modeling
entry.summary: A list of methods for classifying credit applicants and modelling risk. Unlike general machine-learning lists, it gathers papers, datasets and methods specific to credit risk.

entry.title: Awesome Ethereum
entry.summary: A list of developer resources for Ethereum, the smart-contract platform. Unlike general crypto lists, it focuses on smart-contract development — Solidity, development frameworks, testnets.

entry.title: Awesome Ledger
entry.summary: A resource list for double-entry accounting on the command line (Ledger). Unlike accounting apps, the ledger is a plain-text file you can version with git; the list covers Ledger, hledger and Beancount.

entry.title: Awesome Stock Trading
entry.summary: A collection of libraries, strategies and data sources for stock trading. Not investment advice; a list of the tooling in one place.

entry.title: CoinGecko
entry.summary: Market data for thousands of crypto assets, DEXes included, with a free API. Unlike CoinMarketCap (owned by Binance since 2020), it is independent and covers DEXes and small assets more widely.

entry.title: CoinMarketCap
entry.summary: Widely used crypto prices and rankings by market cap. Unlike CoinGecko it has been owned by Binance since 2020 — worth remembering that an exchange owns this data source.

entry.title: DefiLlama
entry.summary: DeFi total-value-locked analytics across chains. Unlike analytics sites with a token of their own it has none and publishes its methodology, which is how it backs its claim to neutrality.

entry.title: Dune
entry.summary: An analytics platform where the community builds dashboards with SQL queries over blockchain data. Unlike block explorers such as Etherscan, you write your own analysis across the whole chain instead of looking at one transaction.

entry.title: Etherscan
entry.summary: Ethereum’s canonical block explorer, with transaction tracing, contract verification and an API. Unlike Dune it is built for inspecting a single transaction, address or contract in detail.

entry.title: Finviz
entry.summary: A visual stock screener that scans the US market on one screen with a heatmap and dense filters. Compared with Yahoo Finance it is for looking across the whole market and filtering, not one stock; real-time data is paid.

entry.title: Glassnode
entry.summary: Crypto market intelligence through on-chain metrics and derived indicators. Unlike price sites it analyses data from the chain itself — wallet flows, supply distribution; most metrics are paid.

entry.title: Investing.com
entry.summary: Multi-asset real-time quotes together with an economic calendar in broad coverage. Compared with Yahoo Finance its economic calendar and coverage of Turkish markets, with a Turkish edition, are stronger.

entry.title: Investopedia
entry.summary: An encyclopedia explaining finance and investing terms dictionary-style, with worked examples. Unlike market-data sites it teaches concepts, not numbers — the place to look when you first meet a term.

entry.title: Koyfin
entry.summary: Bloomberg-like analytics dashboards for equities and macro, offered with a generous free tier.

entry.title: Macrotrends
entry.summary: Free long-term charts of stocks and economic data going back decades. Unlike short-term trading charts it shows the long run — for seeing an indicator in historical context.

entry.title: Musings on Markets (Aswath Damodaran)
entry.summary: Valuation professor Aswath Damodaran’s writing, plus his free datasets — industry margins, cost of capital — updated each January. Unlike brokerage reports it shows its method openly.

entry.title: Nasdaq Data Link (Quandl)
entry.summary: A service aggregating financial and economic data from many sources under one API (formerly Quandl). Instead of pulling scattered sources one by one, you get them through a common interface.

entry.title: Portfolio Visualizer
entry.summary: Runs portfolio backtesting, Monte Carlo simulation and factor analysis in the browser. Unlike building them by hand in a spreadsheet, the analyses come ready with the data; some features are paid.

entry.title: StockAnalysis
entry.summary: Fast, clean stock data and financials with a generous free tier. Compared with Yahoo Finance it has fewer ads, and financial statements are laid out cleanly with longer history.

entry.title: Yahoo Finance
entry.summary: Quotes, financials and portfolio tracking, with free historical price downloads. Unlike paid terminals its free coverage is broad; the trade-off is that the data is mostly delayed.
